newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's post-97 chief heads for Beijing.
newsitem.headline: HK's post-97 chief heads for Beijing.

text.p: Hong Kong shipping tycoon Tung Chee-hwa flies to Beijing on Tuesday for his first meeting with Chinese leaders since he was elected the territory's first post-colonial leader last week.
"My work has started," he told a business dinner party on Monday. "Tomorrow afternoon I will go to Beijing to be formally appointed."
Tung, 59, who was officially named Hong Kong's first post-1997 chief executive by Chinese Premier Li Peng on Monday, is likely to meet Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Wednesday.
Tung was chosen to take over from outgoing London-appointed Governor Chris Patten by a 400-member, Beijing-controlled Selection Committee last week.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 next year after more than 150 years of British rule.
The chief executive-designate's trip comes shortly after the Hong Kong government said it would set limits on how much it would help Tung to form a government-in-waiting.

Secretary for Constitutional Affairs Nicholas Ng told the Legislative Council on Monday the government had ruled out any major secondment of high-ranking officials to the future government being assembled by Tung in the coming weeks.
Whatever secondments were made would not be allowed to undermine stability and efficiency, Ng said.
The colonial administration is to cooperate with the incoming government of the Chinese "Special Administrative Region" under the handover agreement.
But the transition has been fraught with disputes over issues ranging from human rights and democracy to infrastructure projects, darkening prospects for serious cooperation.
Tung greeted Ng's remarks as a sign that cooperation of some sort was in the pipeline.
"I welcome any sort of cooperation from the Hong Kong government. But as for the details, I will start working on them after I am formally appointed," he told reporters.
